questions.question: Direction: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. The reported alarm of the earthquake scared every citizen of the country.

The reported alarm of the earthquake scared every citizen of the country.
questions.solution: "Alarm" is a noun that means a sudden fear or distress caused by danger or threat. "Alarming" is an adjective that means causing alarm or fear. In the sentence, we need an adjective to describe the type of report, not a noun to describe the citizens' reaction. "Alarming report" correctly conveys that the report itself caused fear. Correct sentence: The alarming report of the earthquake scared every citizen of the country.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underline segment in the given sentence. I was carried by her rapturous song.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underline segment in the given sentence.

I was carried by her rapturous song.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'carried away'.

Key Points

  • There is an error in the verb usage in the given sentence.
  • Based on the given options, we need to replace the verb carried with the appropriate phrasal verb. 
  • Let us look into the meanings of the given options - 
    • carried off - to succeed in doing or achieving something difficult
    • carried away - to arouse to a high and often excessive degree of emotion or enthusiasm.
    • carried of - to take or bear (something) from one place to another. (Note - this is not a phrasal verb)
    • carried to - support and move (someone or something) from one place to another. (Note - this is not a phrasal verb)
  • From the above meanings it is clear that carried away is the most appropriate option to substitute the underline segment in the given sentence.
  • Hence, option 2 is the correct answer. 

Correct sentence - I was carried away by her rapturous song.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No improvement’. The Delhi Birla International School alumnus occupy leading positions in different areas of profession and service.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No improvement’.

The Delhi Birla International School alumnus occupy leading positions in different areas of profession and service.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'alumni occupy'.

Key Points

  • The given sentence is in the present indefinite tense. Therefore, option 2 gets eliminated.
  • 'Alumnus' means "a former male student of a school, college or university".
    • E.g. Imran has received numerous job offers because he’s an alumnus of an elite medical school.
  • 'Alumni' means "​the former male and female students of a school, college or university".
    • E.g. Several of the class of 1992 alumni donated money to their classmate’s account when he became ill last winter.
  • The given sentence is not talking about a single student as is clear from 'leading positions in different areas'.
  • Therefore, we cannot use 'alumnus'.  
  • According to the rule and examples that are given above, 'alumni occupy' will be used in the underlined part of the given sentence.
    ​

Correct Sentence: The Delhi Birla International School alumni occupy leading positions in different areas of profession and service.

Additional Information

  • Present Indefinite Tense represents an action which is regular or normal or true and uses the base form of the verb.
  • In the present indefinite tense 's/es' is used with the base form of the verb if the subject is "third-person singular".
    • E.g. My father goes for a walk daily.

questions.solution: The error lies in the part "the more loud they would scream." The correct phrase is 'the louder they would scream' instead of 'the more loud they would scream.' questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No improvement’. Over the past 20 years, there has been a constant decline in the variety of vegetables that we eat because the native varieties are no longer available.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No improvement’.

Over the past 20 years, there has been a constant decline in the variety of vegetables that we eat because the native varieties are no longer available.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is No improvement.

Key Points

  • The present perfect tense is a verb tense that shows an action or state that either occurred at an indefinite time in the past or began in the past and continued to the present time.
  • The structure is given below:
    • Subject + has/have + V3 + object. (active voice)
    • Object + has/have + been + V3 + subject. (passive voice)
  • ​Example:
    • ​He has played some matches for the Indian Cricket team. (active voice)
    • Some matches have been played by him for the Indian Cricket team. (passive voice)
  • In the given sentence, we need to follow the structure in the active voice form.
  • Since the given sentence talks about the action that continues till the present time, 'has been' is the most appropriate choice of the verb form in the underlined part.
  • Thus we are left with the 1st option as the only correct choice.
     

Correct Sentence: Over the past 20 years, there has been a constant decline in the variety of vegetables that we eat because the native varieties are no longer available.

questions.solution: There are two errors in the given sentence. The first error in the sentence is a subject-verb agreement mistake. The auxiliary verb "have" must be used to match the plural subject "people." The second error is the use of an article. The reason for using "the" is that "Philippines" is a proper noun that requires an article when used to refer to a specific country. The use of "the" before "Philippines" helps specify that it is a particular group of people in that country who have voted. Correct sentence: The people of the Philippines have voted to elect a new president.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select 'No substitution'. Commodity prices are dearer in the present economic scenario.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '2' i.e. dear .

Key Points

  • The given sentence aims to describe the current state of commodity prices in the economic scenario.
  • The phrase "the dearer" is incorrect as "dear" itself means expensive. Using "the" before "dearer" is grammatically incorrect in this context.
  • To make the sentence grammatically correct, the word "dear" should be used without any article or comparative form.

Correct sentence: Commodity prices are dear in the present economic scenario.

Additional Information

  • Dear (adjective): This term is used to describe something that is expensive or costly.
  • Comparative and Superlative Forms:
    • Comparative: dearer (used when comparing two things)
    • Superlative: dearest (used when comparing more than two things)

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment In the given sentence. My uncle and his family may come late last night, but I am not sure.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment In the given sentence.

My uncle and his family may come late last night, but I am not sure.
questions.solution:
The correct substitution is "might have come ".

Key Points

  •  As this sentence shows that the person is not sure of the past happening so will use the correct modal words in this case.
  • We use the modal verbs "must-have", "can't have" and "might have" to make guesses or deductions about an action in the past that we believe has definitely happened, has definitely not happened, or possibly happened, based on our knowledge, information or evidence, or lack of it.
  • We use "must-have", "can't have" and "might have" in the same way as the 'present perfect' - 'the action we are describing happened, or did not happen, in the past and is still true in the present'.
  • Usage of only might have -' we believe it's possible that the action happened, but we don't know'.
    • Example: He might have gone to the shops.
  • In the given example, It is possible that he has gone to the shops, but it is also possible that he has gone somewhere else.
  • With the given usage and the example of 'might have' we are sure that this is the most suitable substitution of the given underlined segment in the given sentence.
  • Therefore, the correct answer is option 2.

  • The original sentence is already grammatically correct and conveys the intended meaning effectively. It is written in the past perfect tense, "had just passed", indicating that the birthday had passed a short time before the time of narration.
  • The adverb "unnoticed" correctly describes that nobody except herself acknowledged her birthday.
  • Option 1) changes the meaning of the sentence by using the phrase "but all" instead of "all but." This would mean that everyone noticed her birthday except herself, which is opposite to what is intended.
  • Option 2) uses the present perfect tense, "has just passed", which is not appropriate because the narration is in the past.
  • Option 3) is similar to option 1) by using "but all" instead of "all but." It suffers from the same problem of changing the meaning of the sentence.
  • Therefore, the original sentence is the best choice, and no improvement is required.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select No Improvement. Applications are invite to eligible candidates for the post of Vice-Principal in a reputed school.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select No Improvement.

Applications are invite to eligible candidates for the post of Vice-Principal in a reputed school.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'invited from'

Key Points

  • According to grammar, we need to use 'the third form of the verb invited' after 'are' because 'are' is a linking verb and after the linking verb we usually use the adjective with this adjective 'invited' the correct preposition will be 'from' because 'it indicates the source or provenance' hence the source here is 'eligible candidates' so we need to use 'invited from'

The correct sentence will be - Applications are invited from eligible candidates for the post of Vice-Principal in a reputed school.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution required’. Skydiving was a rare opportunity that I had got, so, even though I was exhausted, I decided to go for it.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution required’.

Skydiving was a rare opportunity that I had got, so, even though I was exhausted, I decided to go for it.
questions.solution: 'No substitution required': The conjunction 'so' here means 'with the result that; therefore'. Example: She felt very tired so she went to bed early. Here, 'even though' means 'although'. The given sentence tells us that 'Although the person was tired yet he tried his hand at skydiving'.

questions.question: Improve the bracketed part of the sentence. Indian restaurants (distributing food) , Indian businesses are throwing open their premises to provide accommodation.
questions.questionHtml:
Improve the bracketed part of the sentence.

Indian restaurants (distributing food), Indian businesses are throwing open their premises to provide accommodation.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is "are distributing food".

Key Points

  • The bracketed part does not contain any helping verb. So, it needs improvement.
  • The verb here must be in Present continuous form as the second part of the sentence is constructed in present continuous form i.e. "are throwing" is used 
  • The use of "were distributing food" and "should distributing food" is incorrect.
  • Thus option 2 is the correct answer.

Correct sentence: Indian restaurants are distributing food, Indian businesses are throwing open their premises to provide accommodation.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment. If there is no need to substitute it, select No improvement. Bulbul is honest girl but she is also very rude.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment. If there is no need to substitute it, select No improvement.
Bulbul is honest girl but she is also very rude.
questions.solution:
The correct solution is option 1.

'an' and 'a' are definite articles whereas 'the' is an indefinite article.

'an' is used when the word starts with a vowel sound - that is, 'a', 'e', 'i', 'o', 'u' and 'a' is used for words starting with a consonant sound.

Here, 'honest', when pronounced, has a sound of 'o' which is a vowel. So, 'an' must be used before 'honest'.

The correct sentence is: Bulbul is an honest girl but she is also very rude.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. Juliet is telling to Ben to complete the work immediately.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

Juliet is telling to Ben to complete the work immediately.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is "telling"

Key Points

  • In the given sentence, the usage of the preposition "to" is incorrect.
  • The preposition 'to' is used to indicate a direction, expression of time, link verb, and phrasal verb.
  • The preposition 'to' is used before verbs as infinitive.
    • Example: To play, to fight, to write.
  • In the given sentence, the verb "telling" is a gerund.
  • The prepositions are usually used before the gerund.
  • The usage of "to" is not adding to the meaning of the sentence and looks like irregular usage.
  • Hence, the correct answer is option 4.
     

The correct sentence is: Juliet is telling Ben to complete the work immediately.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. Josephine confessed that she couldn’t stand another hour out daylight.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

Josephine confessed that she couldn’t stand another hour out daylight.
questions.solution: The given sentence implies that Josephine couldn't endure or tolerate being in daylight for another hour. In English, we typically use "of daylight" to indicate a period or duration during the daytime.  ‘OF’ is a preposition Used for belonging to, relating to, or connected with. Example: The first page of the book describes the author’s profile.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution required’. There was enough evidence to convict him of selling adulterated food.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution required’.

There was enough evidence to convict him of selling adulterated food.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'No substitution required'.

Key Points

  • The given sentence is grammatically correct.
  • In the given sentence the word 'convict' means 'to say officially in a court of law that somebody is guilty of a crime'. (न्‍यायालय द्वारा अपराधी या दोषी ठहराया जाना)
    • Example: He was convicted of armed robbery and sent to prison.
  • We know that the word 'convict' is followed by the preposition 'of'.
  • Here, it is already being followed by 'of'.
  • Hence, no substitution is required.
     

Correct Sentence: There was enough evidence to convict him of selling adulterated food.

Hinglish

  • दिया गया वाक्य व्याकरण की दृष्टि से सही है।
  • दिए गए वाक्य में 'convict' शब्द का अर्थ है 'कानून की अदालत में आधिकारिक तौर पर यह कहना कि कोई व्यक्ति अपराध का दोषी है'।
    • Example: He was convicted of armed robbery and sent to prison.
  • हम जानते हैं कि 'convict' शब्द के बाद 'of' शब्द आता है।
  • इसलिए, कोई प्रतिस्थापन की आवश्यकता नहीं है।

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select No improvement Do you mind to lending me your umbrella?
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select No improvement
Do you mind to lending me your umbrella?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'lending me'

Key Points

  • The given phrase is to be replaced with 'lending me'
  • In the given sentence, 'mind' is the main verb hence after this verb ask a question what? i.e. what does he mind? The answer you'll get is 'lending me your umbrella' Hence, from this, we can say that this is a transitive verb so we need to use a direct object after it.
  • The direct object will be 'noun/pronoun/gerund'
  • The indirect object is 'me'.

So the correct sentence is- Do you mind lending me your umbrella.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select No Improvement. Don’t use those pencils; use the one we bought in Portugal.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select No Improvement.

Don’t use those pencils; use the one we bought in Portugal.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is use the ones.

Key Points

  • Here, 'ones' refer to 'pencils' which is plural, therefore we will use it as it is also plural.
  • A pronoun must agree with its antecedent (the noun to which it refers) in both number and gender.
  • We use 'one' and 'ones' -
    • after an adjective:
      • Example: Which is your car, the red one or the black one? (here, one refers to 'car')
    • after 'the':
      • Example: Let us look at the photographs - the ones you took in Delhi. (here, ones refers to 'photographs')
    • after which in questions:
      • Example: You can have one toy. Which one do you want? (here, one refers to 'toy')
  • Therefore, the most appropriate substitute is 'use the ones'.

questions.question: Improve the underlined part of the sentence. Choose 'No improvement' as an answer if the sentence is grammatically correct. They had to cultivate crops which the company asked them to do.
questions.questionHtml:

They had to cultivate crops which the company asked them to do.
questions.solution: The correct answer is: No improvement. The original sentence is grammatically correct because "had to cultivate crops" correctly expresses the obligation to grow crops as requested by the company.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. No effort has been made by the Indian cricket team t o cash off on its vibrant image in the World Cup.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

No effort has been made by the Indian cricket team to cash off on its vibrant image in the World Cup.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option 4.

To cash off on is a wrong phrase.

The correct phrase is to cash in on. It means to gain an advantage from a situation to make a profit.

The other phrases are incorrect in their usage.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select No improvement. The man who seen the accident to occur telephoned the police.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select No improvement.

The man who seen the accident to occur telephoned the police.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option 3 i.e. "had seen the accident occur".

Key Points

  • The phrase "had seen" correctly implies that the witnessing of the accident occurred before the action of telephoning the police.
  • When two incidents happen in the past one by one, we use past perfect tense for the first incident and simple past for the second incident.
  • Here accident had occurred first then the man telephoned.
  • The structure "had seen the accident occur" correctly uses the past perfect tense to indicate the sequence of events.

Therefore, the correct answer is- "The man who had seen the accident occur telephoned the police."

Additional Information

  •  Option 1 ("saw the accident was occurring") implies that the accident was in the process of happening, but is awkward and does not clearly convey that the action of seeing was completed before he telephoned.
  • Option  2 ("saw the accident occurred") is grammatically incorrect because "saw" and "occurred" do not correctly align in a sequence of events.

questions.question: Direction: Select the word segment that substitutes (replaces) the bracketed word segment correctly and completes the sentence meaningfully. Select the option 'no correction required' if the sentence is correct as given. The ( captain with the members of his team ) failed to qualify for the African Nations Cup finals.
questions.questionHtml:
Direction: Select the word segment that substitutes (replaces) the bracketed word segment correctly and completes the sentence meaningfully. Select the option 'no correction required' if the sentence is correct as given.

The (captain with the members of his team) failed to qualify for the African Nations Cup finals.

options.text: captain along with the members of his team
options.html: captain along with the members of his team

options.text: captain along side the members of his team
options.html: captain along side the members of his team

questions.solution: The word 'with' is redundant in this sentence as 'along with' or 'together with' would have sufficed. 'Captain and his team' is a concise and grammatically correct way to refer to the group. Using 'alongside' instead of 'with' changes the meaning of the sentence, as it implies that the captain and team members were competing against each other. The captain and his team failed to qualify for the African Nations Cup finals.

questions.question: Select the options that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select 'No improvement required'. The probable side effects of this medication include burning and itching .

questions.solution: The verb "include" (plural verb) in the original sentence properly agrees with the subject "side effects", which is plural. 'this medication' is NOT the subject as it is the object of the preposition 'of'.

questions.question: Improve the underlined part of the sentence. Choose 'No improvement' as an answer if the sentence is grammatically correct. We're visited our grandparents on the weekend.
questions.questionHtml:
Improve the underlined part of the sentence. Choose 'No improvement' as an answer if the sentence is grammatically correct.

We're visited our grandparents on the weekend.
questions.solution: The correct answer is: visiting our. The contraction "We're" (We are) requires the present participle "visiting" to form the present continuous tense, which is used here to describe a planned future action.

questions.question: Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select 'No improvement required'. I don't fancy to go out this evening.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select 'No improvement required'.

I don't fancy to go out this evening.
questions.solution: The correct answer is 'going out'. "I fancy" needs a noun/object complement. Thus, participle will be used as the noun complement, which is also termed as 'gerund'. Correct Sentence: I don't fancy going out this evening.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select No improvement. My shoes were worn out so I had to buy a new one.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select No improvement.

My shoes were worn out so I had to buy a new one.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 3 i.e. new ones.

The sentence refers to 'my shoes' meaning they were in plural - the new shoes that one buys would also ideally be in a pair - plural. The original sentence refers to 'a new one' which should be replaced with 'new ones'.

Thus, the correct answer is option 3.
